in_english.name: Raphael
in_english.meaning: God heals, God who heals, God who cures, God who brings salvation
in_english.long_meaning: God, who heals all ailments, and all infirmities, God, who heals all wounds, God, who brings salvation to all, that are under the sun. The name Raphael is derived from the Hebrew words 'Rapha' meaning 'God heals' and 'El' meaning 'God'. In the Bible, Raphael is the name of the archangel who is associated with healing and medicine. In Christian tradition, Raphael is considered a patron saint of nurses, doctors, and healers.

data.cultural_impact: The name Raphael is of significant cultural impact in both the Christian and Jewish traditions. In Christianity, the name is associated with the archangel Raphael, who is renowned as a healer and patron of travelers. In Jewish mythology, Mordecai, a brave Judaean, was given the name Raphael when he was saved from harm, which further emphasizes the healing and protective aspects of the name. The name has also been popularized in various forms of media, including literature and music, where Raphael is often portrayed as a valiant and healing figure.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Raphael carries deep spiritual significance as it is reminiscent of God's healing power. In the Bible, Raphael is a manifestation of God's healing power and compassion. He is an angel of mercy, who not only heals physical ailments but also spiritual wounds. Raphael encourages us to trust in God's ability to bring us back to wholeness and health. Additionally, Raphael's role as a traveler's companion highlights the faith and safety that comes from trusting in God's guidance and protection while on a spiritual journey.
